text: The BS Computer Science Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025 lays out the degree across Semesters 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 7 and 8, showing prerequisites, pre- or corequisites, and the critical path. Grade requirements: a D- or better is required unless noted by *, and a C or better is required in CS 1436, CS 1337, CS 2305, CS 2336 or 2337, MATH 2413 or 2417, MATH 2414 or 2419, and MATH 2418. ECS 1100 Intro to Eng and CS and CS 1200 Introduction to CS and SE are First Year only; transfer students substitute a Technical Elective. ALEKS 80% or MATH 2312 is listed as the starting point for the MATH 2413 or 2417 Calculus I sequence.

section_heading: BS Computer Science Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025: Grade Requirements

text: The core curriculum choices in the BS Computer Science Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025 are: RHET 1302; GOVT 2305; GOVT 2306; two American History (060) courses; Language, Philosophy and Culture (040); Creative Arts (050); and Social and Behavioral Sciences (080) (see the catalog for course options). The major preparatory courses in the plan are: ECS 1100 Intro to Eng and CS; CS 1200 Introduction to CS and SE; CS 1436 Programming Fundamentals; CS 1337 Computer Science I; CS 2305 Discrete Mathematics; CS 2336 (Java) or CS 2337 (C++) Computer Science II; CS 2340 Computer Architecture; MATH 2413 or 2417 Calculus I; MATH 2414 or 2419 Calculus II; MATH 2418 Linear Algebra; PHYS 2325/2125 Mechanics and Lab; and PHYS 2326/2126 Electricity and Magnetism and Lab.
source_title: BS Computer Science Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025
section_heading: BS Computer Science Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025: Core Curriculum and Major Preparatory Courses

text: The upper-division and major courses in the BS Computer Science Eight Semester Plan 2024-2025 are: CS 3341 Probability and Statistics in CS and SE; CS 3345 Data Structures and Algorithms; CS 3377 Systems Programming; CS 4341/4141 Digital Logic Computer Design and Lab; CS 4337 Programming Language Paradigms; CS 3354 Software Engineering; ECS 2390 Professional and Technical Communication; CS 4349 Advanced Algorithm Design and Analysis; CS 3162 Professional Responsibility; CS 4348 Operating Systems Concepts; CS 4384 Automata Theory; CS 4347 Database Systems; and CS 4485 Computer Science Project. The plan also includes Technical Electives (CS 4XXX) and Free Electives, one of which is 1 SCH.
